## Comprehensive Build Prompt

Build a complete, production-ready, mobile-first AI chat web application consisting of a single-page frontend (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, no build step required) and a backend HTTP API that streams AI responses over Server-Sent Events (SSE). Deliver full, unabridged, working source code for every file — no placeholders, no mock data, no simplified stand-ins. The application must run standalone in a browser and communicate with the backend exclusively through the API contract defined below.

### Global Page Structure and Metadata

Create an HTML document with `lang="hu"` (Hungarian) as the primary UI language. Include full responsive viewport meta tags (`width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover, interactive-widget=resizes-content`), PWA metadata (`mobile-web-app-capable`, `apple-mobile-web-app-capable`, `apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style=black-translucent`, `apple-mobile-web-app-title`, `application-name`), dual light/dark `theme-color` meta tags, `color-scheme` set to `dark light`, and `format-detection=telephone=no`. Reference a web app manifest and a full icon set (180, 152, 167, 192 px Apple touch icons plus a generated inline SVG favicon using a rounded-square app-icon glyph). Load a syntax-highlighting library and its stylesheet (dark theme) for code block rendering inside AI responses.

### Visual Design System

Implement a CSS custom-property based theming system supporting both dark and light modes via `prefers-color-scheme`. Define variables for foreground text at three opacities, background color, separator color, hover overlay, and a set of "liquid glass" tokens (semi-transparent gradient layers, border colors, inset highlights, shadow colors, an accent blue/indigo hue, and a send-button glow color). Build a reusable `.lg` "liquid glass" utility class that gives any panel a frosted-glass look: a layered gradient background, a hairline border, multi-layer inset/outset box-shadows, `backdrop-filter: blur(36px) saturate(190%) contrast(1.08) brightness(1.04)` (with `-webkit-` prefix), an isolated stacking context, and two pseudo-elements (`::before` for a soft diagonal highlight using `mix-blend-mode: screen`, `::after` for a subtle inner border glow). All interactive surfaces (sidebar, message input bar, history cards, search-result chip bar) must use this glass treatment.

Disable text selection and native touch callouts globally except inside chat bubbles, markdown content, code blocks, and form fields, where text selection must be explicitly re-enabled. Disable double-tap zoom and touch highlight color on all buttons, links, labels, and icons. Use `-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "SF Pro Text", "SF Pro Display", "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif` as the font stack, with antialiased/legible text rendering.

Render an animated full-viewport background behind the app: a fixed `#bg` layer with a diagonal linear gradient tinted blue/indigo/black at low opacity and heavy blur, plus a second pseudo-layer darkening the composition with a vertical gradient overlay, each with distinct light-mode variants (softer pastel gradients, lighter overlays).

### WebGL Glass Refraction Renderer

Implement an optional WebGL2-based real-time "glass" rendering effect layered as a full-screen canvas (`#glass-renderer-canvas`). It must gracefully no-op if WebGL2 or the `EXT_color_buffer_float` extension is unavailable. Implement it as a multi-pass renderer:

1. A vertex shader producing a full-screen triangle without a vertex buffer (using `gl_VertexID`).
2. A background fragment shader that procedurally renders a slowly animated, palette-shifting radial-blob gradient as the base scene, driven by a time uniform.
3. A separable Gaussian blur fragment shader with a configurable kernel (support kernel radius up to 200, computed via a Gaussian weight function normalized so weights sum to 1), applied first horizontally then vertically to produce a blurred version of the background.
4. A "main" composite fragment shader that: defines any number of rounded-rectangle glass shapes (up to 48) via signed-distance-field rounded-rect functions; computes surface normals of the SDF via finite differences; computes an edge band where the fragment is near the shape boundary; refracts the blurred background texture inside each shape based on the normal direction and a configurable thickness/refraction-factor/dispersion (chromatic aberration by offsetting R, G, B sample points differently); computes a Fresnel-style rim highlight and a directional specular glare band (configurable angle, convergence, hardness, and factor); blends background, refracted/blurred glass, Fresnel highlight, and glare into a final color; and supports numbered debug-output "steps" (distance field, normals, edge mask, blurred texture, refraction-only, Fresnel-only, glare-only, inside-mask, background-only) selectable via a step uniform for development inspection.

Manage two ping-ponged half-float RGBA16F framebuffers plus a background framebuffer, all resized on window resize/DPR change (clamp device pixel ratio to a maximum of 2). Recompute the Gaussian kernel weights whenever the blur radius changes. Expose a single configuration object with tunable parameters: edge thickness, refraction factor, dispersion amount, Fresnel range/hardness/factor, glare range/hardness/factor/convergence/opposite-factor/angle, RGBA tint with alpha, background type, shape width/height/corner radius/roundness, shape-merge rate, and blur radius, plus an animation "step" flag for the render loop.

### Application Shell Layout

Structure the app as a fixed-height (`100dvh`) flex column `#app` containing: a slide-in left `#sidebar` (fixed position, 300px wide, max 85% viewport width, translated off-screen by default, animated in with a spring-like cubic-bezier transition, backed by a semi-transparent blurred panel), a full-screen dimmed `.sb-backdrop` overlay that fades in/out with the sidebar and closes it on tap, a scrollable `#content` region containing `#scroll-area` and `#msg-list`, and a fixed bottom `#ib-wrap` input bar that respects safe-area insets on all four edges (`env(safe-area-inset-*)`).

### Sidebar (Conversation History Panel)

Header row (`.sb-hdr`, 52px tall) with a centered title, a search-toggle icon button, and a close button (both circular, scale-down active states). Below the header, an expandable/collapsible search bar (`#sb-search-bar`) that animates open/closed via height and visibility transitions, containing a rounded search input with a leading magnifier icon and a "Cancel" text button that appears only while the search bar is open.

Below that, a scrollable `.sb-body` containing: a "New Chat" glass button (icon + label) that clears the current conversation and its session id; section labels for grouping conversations (e.g., pinned vs. by recency); and a list (`#hlist`) of history cards (`.hcard`). Each card shows a single-line, ellipsis-truncated preview of the first user message (support inline `<mark>` highlighting of search-matched substrings), a small metadata line (relative timestamp), a delete icon-button that is always visible on touch devices and only visible on hover/focus for pointer devices, and an optional pin indicator icon shown only when the conversation is pinned. Cards must support: single tap to switch conversation, tap on the delete icon to remove that conversation (client list update plus a `DELETE /api/history?session_id=...` backend call, no confirmation dialog blocking the UI), a long-press (500ms on touch, or right-click/`contextmenu` on desktop) that opens a contextual action sheet for a card (rename, pin/unpin, delete), and inline rename via making the title `contenteditable`. Show an empty-state illustration (icon + explanatory paragraph) when there is no history.

Sidebar interactions must support a drag-to-close gesture (tracking touch/pointer movement while `dragging` class disables the CSS transition, then re-enabling the transition and snapping open/closed based on drag distance/velocity), plus a "pull hint" affordance shown near the top while dragging past a threshold.

Persist the full history list to `localStorage`, including per-conversation id, title/preview text, pinned flag, and last-updated timestamp; maintain an in-memory `Map` from session id to array index for O(1) lookups, and re-sort with pinned conversations first, then most-recent-first, on every mutation.

### Main Chat Area

Render messages grouped by consecutive same-role turns inside `.msg-group` (aligned right for user, `class="u"`; aligned left for assistant, `class="a"`). User messages render inside a `.bubble` with a colored gradient background, border, glass blur, and rounded corners (max 85% width). Assistant messages render as `.ai-bubble` with transparent background and no border/shadow (full width), so they read like plain body text rather than a chat bubble. Both bubble types must support inline attached images rendered as rounded thumbnails (`.img-in-msg`) capped at 220×185px with `object-fit: cover`.

Implement a full Markdown renderer (paragraphs, headings h1–h3, ordered/unordered lists, links opening in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, horizontal rules, inline code spans styled as pill-shaped monospace tags, and fenced code blocks). Fenced code blocks must be syntax-highlighted using the loaded highlighting library, matched by language identifier, and rendered inside a `<pre><code>` structure with copy-to-clipboard affordance.

Below every completed assistant message, render an action row (`.t-row`) with icon-text buttons (`.tact`) for at least "copy" (copies the raw content to the clipboard) and "retry" (re-sends the last user turn and regenerates the response) plus a timestamp label (`.btime`). Show a three-dot bouncing "typing" indicator (`.typing` with `.td` dots, staggered animation delays) while waiting for the first token of a new response, and remove it as soon as content starts streaming in.

Support inline live "web/agent search" progress inside an assistant message while it is being generated: on a `search_start` event render a `.srch-wrap` block with a spinning magnifier icon and the literal search query text (label the block "Keresés: <query>" — Hungarian for "Search: <query>"); on `sources`/`search_results` events, populate a horizontally scrollable chip list where each chip is a link showing a favicon (fetched via a favicon service keyed by domain) and the bare hostname (strip leading `www.`), and update a result-count label (Hungarian "N forrás" — "N sources"); on `search_done`, visually mark the search bar as complete (e.g., stop the spinner, add a "done" class).

On any `error` or `warning` streaming event, render a distinct inline error bubble (`.err-bbl`) with a translucent tinted background instead of throwing or silently failing.

If a stream disconnects and is being retried automatically, show a persistent reconnect banner (`.rcn-bar`) with a spinning icon and status text; implement exponential backoff for reconnect attempts (base delay 1500ms, multiplier 1.8, capped at 30000ms) and cancel/clear the banner once a retry succeeds.

### Message Input Bar

Fixed to the bottom of the viewport, containing (top to bottom): an optional horizontally scrollable strip of attached-image thumbnails (`.img-strip`, each thumb 50×50px rounded, with a small circular remove button `.img-rm` overlaid top-right), then an input row (`.ib-row`) with: a circular attach/image-picker icon button, an auto-growing multi-line text input (`contenteditable` or `<textarea>`, growing up to a max height of ~176px, no visible scrollbar, placeholder text, 16px font to avoid iOS zoom-on-focus), and a circular send button with a colored glass gradient background that is disabled (dimmed, non-interactive) whenever the input is empty and no images are attached, and that morphs into a stop/cancel control while a response is streaming.

Pressing send (or hitting Enter without Shift) must: build a payload containing the user's text, any attached images (base64 data URLs or uploaded references), the current session id (or null for a new conversation), and the selected mode/model if applicable; immediately render the user's message bubble and clear the input and attachment strip; then open the streaming request.

### Streaming Protocol (Frontend Consumption)

Implement a `fetch`-based POST to the chat-send endpoint with an `AbortController` for cancellation, reading the response body as a stream via `res.body.getReader()`, decoding UTF-8 chunks incrementally, and parsing them as newline-delimited SSE frames (`event: <type>\ndata: <json>\n\n`) via an incremental buffer parser that only consumes complete frames and retains partial trailing data for the next chunk. Dispatch parsed events to a single handler switching on event type:

- `session`: capture/update the current session id (`sid`/`session_id` field) and persist/re-render history.
- `content`: append the `delta`/`text`/`content` field to a growing buffer, cap the buffer at 256,000 characters (drop oldest), and schedule a throttled re-render via `requestAnimationFrame` with a minimum 70ms interval between DOM updates (re-run Markdown rendering and set `innerHTML` on the message's content node) — never re-render on every single delta to avoid layout thrashing.
- `search_start`, `sources`/`search_results`, `search_done`: render the inline search UI described above.
- `error`/`warning`: render the inline error bubble.
- `done`: mark the stream finished and clear any persisted "active job" marker from `localStorage`.

On stream completion, push the assembled assistant message into the in-memory message array, attach copy/retry action buttons, persist updated history metadata, and auto-scroll to bottom if the user was already near the bottom (do not force-scroll if the user has manually scrolled up to read earlier content). On network/stream failure that is not a deliberate user abort, apply the auto-retry-with-backoff behavior above; on deliberate abort, if partial content was already received, save it as the final assistant message rather than discarding it.

### Job Persistence and Resume-After-Reload

Whenever a send begins, immediately write `{job_id, sid, mode}` to `localStorage` under a fixed key. On every app load, check for a stored active job: query a job-status endpoint; if the job is still running, reconstruct a fresh chat view for that session and reconnect to a resume-streaming endpoint that replays/continues the SSE event stream from where it left off; if the job finished while the tab was closed, clear the stored marker and, if the finished session differs from the currently displayed one, load that session's persisted history instead. Additionally, on load, if there is a currently open session id but no stored job marker, poll a per-session "active job" endpoint to catch jobs that were started from another tab/device.

### Conversation Session Management

Maintain: an in-memory array of message objects `{role, content, ts, imageUrls?}` for the active conversation; a `sid` variable holding the current backend session id (`null` for an unsaved new conversation); functions to start a new chat (abort any active stream, clear the message list DOM and array, optionally clear the session id, clear attachments, reset the input box height); a function to load a conversation by id that fetches its full message history from the backend, rebuilds the DOM (rendering both user and assistant messages, restoring any attached images from either raw URLs or a payload-to-data-URL conversion helper), applies any locally-tracked "deleted message" overrides, and scrolls to the bottom; and a function to switch between conversations that guards against reloading the already-active session. Use monotonically increasing generation counters to guard every async load/stream operation against race conditions from rapid conversation switching (a completed async operation must check it is still the "current" generation before mutating the DOM).

### Backend API Contract

Implement a backend service (any modern server framework) exposing:

- A chat-send endpoint (POST) accepting the message payload (text, optional images, session id or null, mode) and responding with a `text/event-stream` SSE stream emitting the event types listed above (`session`, `content`, `search_start`, `sources`/`search_results`, `search_done`, `error`, `warning`, `done`) as they occur, ultimately persisting the full exchange (user message + assistant message, including any web-search sources used) to durable storage keyed by session id.
- `GET /api/history?session_id=<id>` returning either a bare array of `{role, content, images?, ts}` messages or an object with a `messages` array, representing the full ordered message history for that session.
- `DELETE /api/history?session_id=<id>` permanently deleting that conversation's stored history.
- `GET /api/job/<job_id>/status` returning `{status: "running"|"done", session_id}`.
- `GET /api/session/<session_id>/active_job` returning `{status, job_id, session_id}` describing whether a job is currently running for that session.
- `GET /api/agent/resume/<job_id>` returning a `text/event-stream` that replays/continues the SSE events for an in-progress job so a reconnecting client can resume exactly where a previous connection left off.

All endpoints must handle malformed/missing parameters with proper HTTP status codes and JSON error bodies, must not crash the server process on invalid input, and must be backed by real persistent storage (a real database or durable file-backed store) — no in-memory-only mock persistence, since history must survive server restarts.

### Non-Negotiable Implementation Requirements

Deliver the complete frontend as real, functioning HTML/CSS/JavaScript (not abbreviated snippets) and the complete backend as real, functioning server code implementing every endpoint above with genuine streaming, genuine persistence, and genuine session/job tracking. Every interactive behavior described above (sidebar drag/search/pin/delete/rename, streaming with throttled Markdown re-render, inline search progress chips, auto-retry with backoff, job resume after reload, image attachment and removal, glass visual effects) must be fully implemented and working end-to-end, with no stubbed handlers, no "TODO" placeholders, and no simulated/fake API responses.

### Message Input Bar

Fixed to the bottom of the viewport, containing (top to bottom): an optional horizontally scrollable strip of attached-image thumbnails (`.img-strip`, each thumb 50×50px rounded, with a small circular remove button `.img-rm` overlaid top-right), then an input row (`.ib-row`) with: a circular attach/image-picker icon button (using a native `<input type="file">` file picker, reading files client-side via `FileReader`), an auto-growing multi-line text input (`<textarea>`, growing up to a max height of ~176px, no visible scrollbar, placeholder text, 16px font to avoid iOS zoom-on-focus), and a circular send button with a colored glass gradient background that is disabled (dimmed, non-interactive) whenever the input is empty and no images/files are attached, and that morphs into a stop/cancel control while a response is streaming.

Implement client-side image compression before attaching: decode the image via an offscreen `<canvas>`, downscale to a maximum dimension (default 1024px), and re-encode as JPEG at a configurable quality (default 0.82), skipping compression for GIF/WebP/APNG/SVG sources. Support pasting images directly from the clipboard into the input, and support attaching arbitrary text files by reading their contents with `FileReader.readAsText` and rendering them as removable file chips that get inlined as fenced code blocks in the outgoing message text.

Pressing send (or hitting Enter without Shift) must: build a payload containing the user's text, any attached images (as base64 data URLs) and any attached file contents inlined as code blocks, and the current local conversation id (or generate a new one); immediately render the user's message bubble and clear the input and attachment strip; then open the streaming request directly from the browser to the configured chat-completion endpoint.

### Streaming Protocol (Direct Client-to-API Communication)

Implement a `fetch`-based POST directly from the browser to a configurable external chat-completion API endpoint, using an `AbortController` for cancellation, reading the response body as a stream via `res.body.getReader()`, decoding UTF-8 chunks incrementally, and parsing them as newline-delimited SSE frames (`event: <type>\ndata: <json>\n\n`) via an incremental buffer parser that only consumes complete frames and retains partial trailing data for the next chunk. Dispatch parsed events to a single handler switching on event type:

- `content`: append the `delta`/`text`/`content` field to a growing buffer, cap the buffer at 256,000 characters (drop oldest), and schedule a throttled re-render via `requestAnimationFrame` with a minimum 70ms interval between DOM updates (re-run Markdown rendering and set `innerHTML` on the message's content node) — never re-render on every single delta to avoid layout thrashing.
- `search_start`, `sources`/`search_results`, `search_done`: render the inline search UI described above, if the endpoint emits these event types.
- `error`/`warning`: render the inline error bubble.
- `done`: mark the stream finished.

On stream completion, push the assembled assistant message into the in-memory message array, attach copy/retry action buttons, persist the full updated conversation (including the new turn) to `localStorage`, and auto-scroll to bottom if the user was already near the bottom (do not force-scroll if the user has manually scrolled up to read earlier content). On network/stream failure that is not a deliberate user abort, apply the auto-retry-with-backoff behavior above; on deliberate abort, if partial content was already received, save it as the final assistant message rather than discarding it.

Expose a simple settings mechanism (a small settings panel or `localStorage`-backed configuration) where the API endpoint URL, API key/token, and model identifier can be entered and stored client-side, and used as headers/body fields on every outgoing request; never hardcode secrets into the shipped source.

### Conversation Session Management (Client-Side Only)

Maintain: an in-memory array of message objects `{role, content, ts, imageUrls?}` for the active conversation; a `sid` variable holding the current local conversation id (`null` for an unsaved new conversation, generated client-side once the first message is sent); functions to start a new chat (abort any active stream, clear the message list DOM and array, clear the session id, clear attachments, reset the input box height); a function to load a conversation by id that reads its full message history from `localStorage`, rebuilds the DOM (rendering both user and assistant messages, restoring attached images from stored data URLs), and scrolls to the bottom; and a function to switch between conversations that guards against reloading the already-active session. Use monotonically increasing generation counters to guard every async load/stream operation against race conditions from rapid conversation switching (a completed async operation must check it is still the "current" generation before mutating the DOM).

### Non-Negotiable Implementation Requirements

Deliver the complete application as real, functioning HTML/CSS/JavaScript (not abbreviated snippets), containing zero backend/server code, zero server-side endpoints, and zero server-side persistence — every piece of state (conversation history, settings, attachments) must be stored and managed entirely in the browser. Every interactive behavior described above (sidebar drag/search/pin/delete/rename, streaming with throttled Markdown re-render, inline search progress chips, auto-retry with backoff, image/file attachment and removal, glass visual effects) must be fully implemented and working end-to-end, with no stubbed handlers, no "TODO" placeholders, and no simulated/fake responses — the only external call permitted is the direct client-to-API streaming request described above.
